title: cost optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: Adds an end-to-end autotune pipeline that proposes and applies safe default batching and KV-caching parameters, generates quantization profiles for common model families, and surfaces unit-economics estimates in the Console and CLI. Motivation: Customers consistently ask for recommended defaults and automated tuning to reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs. This work unifies three high-impact levers: batching, caching, and quantization, and ties them to unit-econ estimates so teams can make informed tradeoffs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces an autotune coordinator service that analyzes request traces (sampled) and recommends batching window, max_batch_size, and cache prefix heuristics.
- Adds safe rollout logic: recommendations are applied as defaults for new deployments and exposed as suggestions in the Console before switching.
- Adds model-family quantization profiles (fp16/int8/e4M) generator and a compatibility matrix that maps model variants to candidate quant profiles.
- Extends unit-economics tooling to estimate cost-per-1k-tokens given batching/caching/quant settings; integrates this into the Console route configuration UI and CLI reports.
- Provides migration scripts to backfill profile suggestions for existing Dedicated pools.

Checklist: 
- [x] Autotune coordinator service and CRD
- [x] Recommendation engine with safety constraints and canary rollout
- [x] Quantization profile generator and compatibility matrix
- [x] Console UI: suggestions & unit-econ panel
- [x] CLI: redwood optimize report command
- [x] End-to-end tests (unit + integ + perf regression)
- [x] Docs: design doc + user guide

Backward compat / safety: All recommendations are opt-in for existing routes. When the recommendation is applied automatically it is first staged behind a canary flag per-customer and the rollout uses traffic-splitting with automatic rollback on error rate or latency regressions. Quant profiles are suggestions by default and require explicit pinning to change the runtime artifact.

Testing and perf results:
- Synthetic workload (mix of short chat and long completions) shows median token cost reduction 18% (95% CI 15-21%) on GPT-like 7B family using int8 quant + batching defaults.
- Latency SLOs maintained: p95 generation latency change +2% (within SLO).
- Integration tests: 56 new unit tests, 6 integration scenarios; CI run passed after two fixes.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to 10% of orgs for 48 hours, monitor unit-econ delta, error rate, and Console feedback. If negative signals observed revert via rollout controller.

Design notes and alternatives considered: We debated fully-automated vs suggestion-first models. Given risk profile we implemented suggestion-first with an opt-in automated path guarded by canary rules. Quantization profiles are generated conservatively to avoid measurable quality regressions; the config includes a quality threshold derived from eval harness baselines.
commits: feat(autotune): add coordinator and recommendation engine
feat(quant): generate compatible quantization profiles and matrix
feat(cli): `redwood optimize report` and recommendation apply command
chore(tests): add unit and integration tests for autotune flows
fix(ci): increase timeout for perf integration job
review_comments:
Ethan Zhang (reviewer): Can we ensure the recommendation window respects per-customer latency SLO overrides?
Author (Ava): Yes — recommender reads route-level SLOs and constraints before proposing changes; added tests (recommender_test.py) to cover that.

Priya Nair (reviewer): The quant profile generator looks aggressive for T5-like models — what is the rollback path if we see quality regressions?
Author (Ava): We only propose quant profiles that pass our eval-harness baselines (0.5% BLEU/rescaled metric threshold). When applied we stage them in canary and capture eval samples; added automatic rollback trigger based on eval delta and customer feedback.

Liam O'Connor (approver): CI flaked once on perf tests; confirmflaky fixed?
Author (Ava): Fixed the tunable timeout and added idempotent mocks; CI green on rerun.

Post-merge note from SRE (Jordan Kim): Please monitor dedicated pools for increased memory pressure after canary rollout; we've added alerts.

All reviewers: approved with minor nits addressed.
release_notes: Autotune: automatic suggestions for batching and caching defaults; quantization profile generation for supported model families; Unit-economics estimates added to Console and CLI (redwood optimize report). Rollout is staged and opt-in for existing routes.
